unverifiable_exemptions: Owner-occupied property of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit as their primary residence
Units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back under BMC 13.76.130 A.9
Units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates
coverage.summary: Applies to rental housing providers in Berkeley as to current and prospective tenants. No unit-count or construction-date limits are stated. Owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit as their primary residence are exempt. Public housing/Section 8 properties have limited exemptions. Some tenancy-specific exemptions also apply.
coverage.owner_conditions: Exempt if the property is owner-occupied with between 1 and 3 units and an owner of record lives in one of the units as their primary residence.

evidence.quoted_span: Owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence
Owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence

The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
It is unlawful to do any of the following with regard to current or prospective tenants
Owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence
Units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back to their home in accordance with BMC 13.76.130 A.9
Units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates

result.notes: Changed requires_unknown_facts from true to false. The ordinance covers ordinary rental housing citywide, and its exemptions are listed under unverifiable_exemptions instead. Removed the summary claim that the ordinance is stricter than and adds to state FEHA criminal-history rules, because no document supports it. Coverage is based on the Rent Board overview page (D003), not the ordinance text, which D003 says contains the specific requirements for each exemption.
